answer: Sybil farms fail when identity is costly to age, not merely to create. Each applicant must park a relic bond that stays clawable for many epochs and cannot be split or reused across keys. Voting weight then moves only down a river of delayed counterparty hops; each hop adds a wait, so new accounts cannot vote as they appear. A public prism of those hops—payer graphs, unlock clocks, treasury origins—shows clones as the same refraction, then the bond is slashed and leftover streams burn. Parallel copies spend separate aged capital and still cluster, a net loss versus one slow, clean identity.
